articles.title: Ludmilla investe no EP folião 'Fervo da Lud' assim que lançar álbum ao vivo com a gravação do show 'Fragmentos' | G1
articles.body:
Ludmilla estreia na gravadora Sony Music com o EP carnavalesco 'Fervo da Lud' — Foto: Reprodução / Facebook Ludmilla

♬ Em outubro, Ludmilla lançará álbum audiovisual com o registro ao vivo do show “Fragmentos – A experiência”, captado em julho em apresentação da cantora no Rio de Janeiro (RJ), na estreia do espetáculo inspirado no álbum “Fragmentos” (2005).

A gravação audiovisual será exibida primeiramente nos cinemas, em sessões programadas para 6 de outubro, véspera do lançamento do álbum “Fragmentos – A experiência – Ao vivo” nos aplicativos de áudio e nos canais de vídeo da artista.

Contudo, uma vez lançado o álbum, Ludmilla já parte na sequência para o próximo projeto fonográfico da carreira. A cantora debutará na gravadora Sony Music com o EP “Fervo da Lud”, trabalho de clima folião, inspirado pelo bloco comandado pela cantora no Carnaval carioca.

Aliás, o bloco já tem apresentações agendadas no Carnaval 2027 das cidades de Rio de Janeiro (RJ) e Salvador (BA). A intenção da cantora é promover várias ações de marketing para turbinar o EP “Fervo da Lud” e esquentar o clima para o Carnaval.

articles.title: Tiffany Trump’s Toddler Son Looks Adorably Confused in Mom’s Chic Photos
articles.summary: Tiffany Trump often shares special moments with her followers, and her latest photo dump offers another glimpse into her family life. The snapshots from a re...
articles.body:
Tiffany Trump shared photos from her recent trip to India featuring her toddler son Alexander, who looked slightly puzzled in the family snapshots.

The photos included Tiffany's husband Michael Boulos, her mother Marla Maples, and showcased Tiffany wearing a custom Manish Malhotra lehenga for the Ganesh Chaturthi celebration in Mumbai.

Tiffany Trump often shares special moments with her followers, and her latest photo dump offers another glimpse into her family life. The snapshots from a recent trip include her toddler son, Alexander , who adds an adorable touch to the family album. The toddler's expression, however, is hard to miss.

Tiffany Trump's toddler son is just along for the ride in mom's photos from India

Tiffany shared the photos on Instagram with the simple caption, "India, with love." The carousel featured her husband, Michael Boulos, her mother, Marla Maples, and their son, Alexander, during their time in Mumbai.

In one photo, the toddler looks slightly puzzled as he sits with the family, giving the otherwise polished pictures a more candid feel. He wore a red kurta with white pants. Tiffany's outfit also stood out. She wore a custom Manish Malhotra lehenga for the Ambani family's Ganesh Chaturthi celebration at Antilia in Mumbai.

The pastel lime/pistachio-green lehenga featured a cropped blouse and flowing skirt with delicate floral embroidery. The intricate detailing added texture to the otherwise soft palette, while the coral-pink dupatta brought a brighter pop of color. Tiffany finished the traditional look with statement jewelry and a maang tikka.

Michael also embraced the occasion in traditional Indian clothing, wearing a copper-toned sherwani with cream trousers. The September trip marks Tiffany's second visit to India this year.

In May, she and Boulos toured several well-known destinations, including Delhi's Akshardham Temple, the Taj Mahal in Agra , and Jaisalmer in Rajasthan. Tiffany later described her Taj Mahal visit as "an incredible visit" and "a dream come true."

Tiffany continues to give followers occasional glimpses into her life as a mom while keeping most family moments away from the spotlight. Fans also reacted warmly to her latest update, with one commenter calling her a "Punjabi queen."

articles.title: Carly Rae Jepsen's dreamy double album, 'Day and Night,' out tomorrow, proves she's right where she wants to be
articles.summary: Jepsen was catapulted to fame with "Call Me Maybe." Nearly 15 years later, she's taking things at her own pace.
articles.body:
Carly Rae Jepsen just gets it. The Canadian pop singer-songwriter is gearing up to release her eighth studio album, Day and Night , on Friday. The lengthy 24-track project is also a double album that offers an honest, introspective look at how differently she responds to music during the day and at night. Where Day is "more organic," Night is "synth-based" and "gets a little bit more experimental," according to Jepsen . Both sides of the album, she assured, are equally as dreamy.

"This album has two sides and if I could perfume it in a bottle for you, Day would be like jasmine star or daffodils when you really get your nose in there. And Night would be the ocean breeze, pine and citrus," Jepsen wrote on Instagram .

Jepsen initially announced Day and Night in June, a project she's described as being a dream come true. The British Columbia native had no intention of making a double album, which she likened, in an interview with Range magazine , to a "stream of consciousness poem." It just sort of happened.

"I just liked the idea of making the music I wanted to listen to, and I was drawn to these two really different lanes," Jepsen said. "There's just two different directions. They belong together because they encapsulate where I'm at right now musically, and one without the other doesn't really capture the full picture."

She's since debuted four singles from Day and Night : " On Wires ," a piano-heavy track about yearning; " After All ," a loved-up, disco-infused offering about married life and motherhood; " Don't Leave Me on the Dance Floor ," a groovy, ABBA-inspired track about fears of abandonment; and " Motivation ," Jepsen's joyous, electro-pop "family anthem."

"I feel like in order to write about love or heartbreak or any emotion, you just have to have felt it," Jepsen told Vogue of her approach to songwriting. "I have to know what I'm talking about emotionally, or I'm not going to be able to write for shit. From there it can get a bit playful. It may not have been raining or that may not have been exactly what was said, but it certainly felt that way."

For Jepsen, this moment was, in many respects, decades in the making. She may have burst onto the American music scene with support from fellow Canadian pop star Justin Bieber in 2011 (see: Bieber and Selena Gomez's iMac video that changed millennial lives), but every move she's made thereafter has been distinctly her own. Now, at 40, Jepsen is married, blissfully in love and raising her first child, all while writing and releasing new music and crafting the score for Lena Dunham's upcoming 10 Things I Hate About You Broadway musical .

"Where I've landed now in my career is the sweet spot," Jepsen told the Hollywood Reporter . "I can live a life, go to the grocery store, have a family, tour music that I love and have an audience. That's a very hard-earned, balanced thing that we've had to work at."

Before establishing herself as a low-key pop singer-songwriter who casually drops a handful of bangers every few years, Jepsen was known for her track, " Call Me Maybe ," which went viral in a burgeoning social media era. There was no TikTok, but there was YouTube, Twitter (before its X rebrand) and the radio. Bieber heard the track on a Canadian radio station while visiting family in Ontario in December 2011. The "Baby" pop star, who was just 17 at the time, tweeted after hearing the song, "Call me maybe by Carly Rae Jepsen is possibly the catchiest song I've ever heard lol."

In February 2012, Jepsen signed with Scooter Braun's Schoolboy Records and was catapulted to international fame. She released her second studio album, Kiss, in September 2012, embarked on her own tour and served as a supporting act on Bieber's Believe tour until March 2013.

Jepsen has spoken at length about her difficulties in navigating a career post-"Call Me Maybe" and the mounting pressure to release an equally good, if not better, follow-up to escape one-hit-wonder allegations. It would've been easy for Jepsen to get swept up in the trappings of a sudden, whirlwind catapult to fame. In those moments, Jepsen said she thought of why she pursued music in the first place, telling the Hollywood Reporter , "If I'm being honest, I felt a little voice from inside screaming at me to hold on to why I started."

Jepsen added of her sudden success, "It was so overnight that I feel like I understand what it must be like for some people who live in that space consistently, and my heart goes out to them. I'm just not very good at it."

Then came the release of Emotion, Jepsen's third studio album, in 2015. Tapping into nostalgic '80s synth-pop and earnest songwriting, the album has been widely regarded as a modern pop masterpiece. The Emotion era was marked by Jepsen's jet-black mullet and a desire to feel tough, as she told Vulture , "I wanted to feel less worried about how I was perceived by anyone other than myself."

Jepsen's lead single, " I Really Like You ," an infectious, synth-pop track about having a major crush, was accompanied by a viral, feel-good music video starring Tom Hanks. Her follow-up singles, "Run Away with Me," "Your Type" and "Boy Problems" garnered similar praise.

Jepsen had officially established herself as a mainstay in pop music. More importantly, she was having fun while doing it.

"I needed to figure out what else I had to offer to pop music. And with Emotion , I feel like I really started to find my people and everything just became more fun," Jepsen told Vogue . "It took [away] a little bit of the fear of needing my music to be the biggest thing in the world, versus something that I'm excited about."

Day and Night is a sprawling album that dives into life's twists and turns and the confusing, at times overwhelming, feeling that comes during periods of transition. In the nearly 15 years since her international breakthrough, Jepsen has defined and refined her pop sensibilities. She's established herself as a cult- favorite pop singer-songwriter in her own right and has built a life of her own choosing — a family on her own terms.

"There was something liberating about turning 40 and feeling like I can do whatever I want now," Jepsen told Vogue . "If not now, then when?"

Jepsen has finally struck the perfect balance: a life that works for her.

articles.title: Shailene Woodley's stylist responds to 'super rude and mean' reaction to the actor's Emmys outfit
articles.summary: In a pair of social media posts, Karla Welch hit back at critics who panned the "Paradise" star's red carpet look.
articles.body:
Shailene Woodley's stylist has responded to the harsh criticism that the actress received for her Emmy Awards outfit — a periwinkle halter top, gold sequined pants and long burgundy gloves — created by Balenciaga creative director Pierpaolo Piccioli.

"Love or hate something fine but it's an opinion and it can even be a conversation but being super rude and mean and taking glee from it, well that says a lot more about the mouths it's coming from," Karla Welch wrote on Threads Tuesday alongside a black heart emoji.

On Wednesday, the stylist, who has worked with Olivia Wilde, Elisabeth Moss and Justin and Hailey Bieber, also posted a photo to Instagram of Woodley's couture look. The image was preceded by a slide saying "Trigger Warning."

Woodley won her first career Emmy, taking home the award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series for her role in Paradise at the Creative Arts Emmys on Sept. 6. At that ceremony, she wore a Brandon Maxwell-designed white minidress.

For Monday's Emmys telecast, Woodley showed up on the red carpet in an ensemble that drew criticism online , including comparisons to an outfit chosen by ChatGPT.

"Shailene Woodley appears to have played closet roulette," Yahoo's Kerry Justich wrote .

Woodley wore the outfit onstage to present the Emmy for Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series.

At one point inside the Peacock Theater, Woodley was photographed wearing a black blazer alongside Nicole Kidman, her Big Little Lies costar.

For Disney's Emmys afterparty, Woodley showed up sans gloves in a vintage T-shirt promoting the 1986 film Home of the Brave . But she still had on those gold sequined pants.

articles.title: Lady Gaga and Michael Polansky Welcomed a Baby Girl, and Her Name Has a Special Musical Connection (Exclusive Source)
articles.summary: PEOPLE confirmed on Sept. 11 that Gaga and fiancé Michael Polansky welcomed their first baby
articles.body:
Lady Gaga and fiancé Michael Polansky recently welcomed a baby girl named Rose Bean Polansky

The name Rose is inspired by Gaga's connection to "La Vie En Rose," which she covered in A Star Is Born , a source tells PEOPLE

Sources say Gaga is thrilled to be a mom and is enjoying time away from the spotlight with her baby

Following news that the musician, 40, and her fiancé Michael Polansky, 42, recently became parents, sources tell PEOPLE that the couple welcomed a baby girl named Rose Bean Polansky. TMZ was first to report the news.

An insider tells PEOPLE that the name Rose is inspired by the song "La Vie En Rose," which Gaga famously covered in the 2018 movie A Star Is Born. The "Born This Way" artist also has a large tattoo on her spine of a single rose on a long stem with the words, "la vie en rose" written in script beside it.

Rose's middle name Bean likely comes from activist Carl Bean, who inspired Gaga's song "Born This Way," adds the source.

Reps for the couple have not confirmed or commented on the baby's sex or name.

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

PEOPLE confirmed on Sept. 11 that the "Abracadabra" hitmaker and her fiancé welcomed a child.

Shortly after news broke about the baby, sources told PEOPLE that Gaga "sounds very happy."

"She always wanted to be a mom. This was something very important to her," the insider close to the 16-time Grammy winner told PEOPLE exclusively.

The source added that Gaga "was ready to slow down after her tour," which wrapped in April.

"Right now, she's enjoying being away from the public eye and having this special time with the baby," the source continued. "Michael is great with the baby. They're figuring everything out together. She doesn't want to miss any of it."

Another source previously told PEOPLE that the couple "took time off of work this summer to be with [the] baby."

The pair were first photographed kissing at a 2020 New Year's Eve party in Las Vegas, and they went public with their relationship shortly after the 2020 Super Bowl in Miami, PEOPLE previously reported.

Polansky, an entrepreneur and Harvard University graduate, quarantined with Gaga at her Malibu home during the COVID-19 pandemic. Gaga confirmed her and Polansky's engagement in July 2024 when she introduced the tech entrepreneur as her "fiancé," while talking to French Prime Minister Gabriel Attal at the Paris Olympics. He has also collaborated with Gaga on her 2025 album Mayhem, co-producing the record and co-writing several songs.

Gaga has been open about her desire to become a mom over the past several years.

In a December 2019 YouTube video with NikkieTutorials, the "How Bad Do U Want Me" musician said her 10-year plan included having children.

"I want to do more movies," she said at the time. "I want to have babies."

articles.title: Ed Sheeran faces growing backlash as radio station bans songs, protest groups respond to Macklemore's removal
articles.summary: Classic Hits Radio announced it will stop playing Ed Sheeran's music after backlash over Macklemore's removal from the Loop Tour over Gaza protests.
articles.body: Ed Sheeran continues to deal with the backlash surrounding Macklemore's removal from the singer’s U.S. tour. An Irish radio station announced Thursday that, in response to the controversy and feedback from listeners, it would no longer play music released by the 35-year-old "Shape of You" singer for the "foreseeable future." Dave Kelly, group program director at Bay Broadcasting, which runs Classic Hits Radio, told The Independent the decision "has been carefully considered" and "is not intended as a personal judgment on Ed Sheeran." "We acknowledge his own explanation of the circumstances surrounding recent events," Kelly said. "As an independent Irish-owned radio station, however, we believe it is important to listen to our audience and to stand alongside Irish artists who have made what is undoubtedly a significant professional decision based on their own convictions." ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO He added his company "believe(s) in peace, humanity and respect" as well as "the right of people and artists to express and act upon their sincerely held views." "In light of the strength of feeling expressed by our listeners and the decisions taken by Irish artists involved in the tour, we believe removing Ed Sheeran’s music from our playlist is the appropriate decision for Classic Hits Radio at this time," he concluded. The controversy began after Macklemore repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song, "Hind’s Hall," during his opening performance at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, Sept. 4 and 5. Advertisement He was then dropped as an opening act on Sheeran's Loop Tour. The "Thrift Shop" singer alleged that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft pressured Sheeran into dropping him from the tour, telling the singer he would not be allowed to perform at Gillette Stadium and by encouraging other stadium owners to issue a similar ultimatum. Following Macklemore's removal from the tour, four other supporting acts chose to drop out, including Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga, Lukas Graham and Finneas. In addition to the radio station's decision to temporarily remove his music from its catalog, the pro-Palestine groups Philly Palestine Coalition and Shut Down D&Z have planned a protest outside of Sheeran's Philadelphia concert. They shared a flyer on Instagram urging people to attend the protest on Sept. 19 outside Lincoln Financial Field. The flier reads, "Gaza is our compass" and "Billionaires, Zionists & Warmongers out of Philly." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "Palestine returns to headlines across the world and we return to the streets to fight for Gaza. Free Palestine is not a tagline for celebrities or a slogan for online statements," they wrote in the caption. "A free Palestine is the work of generations of Palestinian resistance, a free Palestine is the compass for all oppressed people, a free Palestine demands nothing less than total liberation. Free Palestine is a call to direct action. On Saturday, we take to the streets to return the conversation to Palestine, and return Philadelphia to action." They continued, writing that Sheeran removed Macklemore from his tour "in the name of 'neutrality' and being 'apolitical' and due to threats from stadium owners, including Lincoln Financial Field." "There is no neutrality against oppression, only complicity. When the news cycle has moved on, we will still be here. Join us. FREE PALESTINE, FREE LEBANON, FREE CUBA, FREE CONGO, FREE SUDAN." Sheeran addressed the controversy on Instagram, writing, "I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "After Macklemore’s performances at my New Jersey shows, venues on my upcoming tour dates communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting," Sheeran wrote. "I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said. "I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft. I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue’s and promoter’s decision was final." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE He added that the decision to remove Macklemore from the tour was the promoter's and that "Macklemore’s contract for the tour was with the promoter, not me." "There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds," he added. "Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace. "I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change." articles.title: Ms. Rachel Matches Macklemore’s $1 Million Donation to Support Palestine: ‘We Have a Moral Obligation’
articles.summary: Ms. Rachel, whose real name is Rachel Accurso, shared she is matching Macklemore's $1 million dollar donation to help support Palestine.
articles.body:
Children's show host Ms. Rachel, whose real name is Rachel Accurso, shared that she is matching Macklemore's $1 million donation to help support Palestine. She also challenged "every wealthy white celebrity" to join her, adding that she views it as a "moral obligation."

"I will match Macklemore's donation and I invite every wealthy white celebrity to match it and speak out against the genocide in Gaza," Accurso posted Thursday on Instagram . "Over 20,000 precious Palestinian children have been killed and children continue to be killed every day. We have a moral obligation to use our privilege and platforms to protect children and human rights."

The YouTuber also noted in her caption that she is an ambassador for the Palestine Children's Relief Fund (PCRF) and will be donating to the organization.

On Wednesday, Macklemore said he would be donating his entire $1 million in earnings from opening for Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour to organizations supporting Palestine. He also challenged Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft to do the same. This followed opening acts Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and house band Beoga dropping out in solidarity with Macklemore's dismissal, leaving the remainder of Sheeran's tour without an opener.

"With everything that has happened over the last 48 hours, I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom," Macklemore wrote. "I will be donating the entire $1 million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour to six organizations working directly to support the Palestinian people. And I invite Robert Kraft to match my donation. Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting. A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this earth." Kraft responded later Wednesday pledging $2 million to aid Gaza's "humanitarian crisis" in the region . The Kraft Group executive said that his donation came as a match to Sheeran's own $2 million commitment, as the Grammy winner reportedly rallied support from other stadium owners who did not want Macklemore performing on their properties.

"I have dedicated much of my life to building bridges between all people," Kraft wrote in a statement shared to Gillette Stadium's official X account . "I believe deeply that all lives are worth protecting. Earlier today, before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit $2 million to match his donation to aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis. Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges."

This isn't the first time Accurso has weighed in on the Sheeran/Macklemore controversy. On Monday, she called out the singer for dropping the rapper from his tour.

"Ed Sheeran had an opportunity [to] show that we won't be bullied into punishing people for supporting Palestine," she wrote. "Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows. A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak out against it. If more than 20,000 white children were killed in another part of the world, everyone would be shouting about it at their concerts. Treating some children's lives as less worthy of outrage is racist. Silence during a genocide is not neutral."

articles.title: Venezia vs Lazio | Where to Watch, Insights, Lineups & Prediction
articles.summary: In the final Serie A round before the international break, Lazio will travel north to take on the newly promoted Venezia.Venezia vs Lazio: Kick-Off Time, Loc...
articles.body:
In the final Serie A round before the international break, Lazio will travel north to take on the newly promoted Venezia.

Venezia vs Lazio: Kick-Off Time, Location & Where to Watch

The Serie A clash between Venezia and Lazio kicks off at 20:45 local time on Saturday, September 19, at the Pier Luigi Penzo Stadium in Venice.

To find out how to watch Venezia vs Lazio in your respective country, check out this verified list of international TV listings .

Venezia Form Guide: Recent Results & Table Position

After winning the Serie B title and bolstering their ranks with exciting new arrivals, some backed Venezia to be the top flight's Dark Horse this season. But after the first four rounds of the season, Giovanni Stroppa's men are still seeking their first point.

The Arancioneroverdi began their Serie A campaign with a home defeat to Lecce in an early relegation scrap, before suffering another 0-2 defeat at home to AC Milan . The Venetians then fell short in an action-packed 2-3 defeat to fellow newly promoted Frosinone, while their last league appearance saw them lose 2- 4 to Fiorentina courtesy of hat-trick hero Franco Mastantuono .

Venezia thus find themselves at the very bottom of the Serie A table, as they remain the only club that has yet to get off the mark.

Lazio Form Guide: Recent Results & Table Position

While Venezia have yet to record a defeat, Lazio boast an almost perfect record, registering 10 points from their first four matches, placing them fourth in the standings. The Biancocelesti dropped points for the first time last weekend, when they squandered a two-goal lead to settle for a 2-2 draw with Milan.

Takeaways From Lazio's Draw vs Milan: Belahyane Can Become a Starter

Gennaro Gattuso's men had prevailed in their previous three league fixtures, recording 1-0 wins over Bologna and Genoa , before completing a come-from-behind victory in Udine thanks to Albert Gudmundsson 's winner.

Lazio's recent record against Venezia: The Biancocelesti haven't suffered a defeat in their last nine meeting with the Lagunari across all competitions, registering six wins and three draws.

Lazio's unbeaten run: Lazio have the opportunity to extend their unbeaten run in Serie A to six games in a row for the first time since November 2026.

Venezia (3-5-2): Stankovic; Schingtienne, Moreno, Juan Jesus ; Hainaut, Kike Perez, Basic, Sohm , Haps ; Yeboah, Adams.

Lazio (4-3-3): Mandas; Floriani Mussolini , Sutalo, Provstgaard, Tavares; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Cancellieri , Pinamonti , Zaccagni.

Final Score Prediction: Venezia 1-2 Lazio

Despite what the table standings might suggest, this won't be a walk in the park for Lazio, as Venezia have the tools to inflict damage, even if they haven't been able to come out with the right results. Therefore, Gattuso's men must be prepared to grind to return to Rome with all three points in the bag.

The Calabrian has been operating with limited options in midfield, but he now possesses healthy depth in attack, so one of the second-half substitutes could end up winning it for the Aquile.

articles.title: Miley Cyrus Describes Last Conversation With Dolly Parton, Prompted by Sending Over Her New Album: ‘Though We Were So Different, That’s What Made Us Perfect for Each Other’
articles.summary: Miley Cyrus, now being professionally known as just Miley, spoke about her last conversation with her godmother, Dolly Parton — stemming from Cyrus sending P...
articles.body:
Miley Cyrus, now being professionally known as just Miley, spoke about her last conversation with her godmother, Dolly Parton — stemming from Cyrus sending Parton an advance copy of her new album, "Bass Persuades" — in a fresh interview with Zane Lowe.

"Dolly has been the first person that when I get a vinyl printed," Parton told the Apple Music podcast host. "That's the first person I send it to since I've been making vinyls, and this time around I was going to send her a vinyl because I always do. I'm just trying to keep myself together, but the time that we talked, which was the last time we would talk, it was actually me telling her about this record because even though we are so different, that's what made us so perfect for each other, It's that — and she knew this, and I know this — she is known for the fake, the hair, the makeup, and the show of it. But there's a part of her that I think is what everyone gravitates towards… how real she is and how authentic she is.

"And there was a time in my life — we hit on it with Hannah (Montana) — so much of my life was about persona. And I think a way that I could look at that as you can have a persona and still be who you are is because I had Dolly. Sometimes I call what I do drag because the way that I present myself is just someone that is so different from the person that feeds the tortoise every morning. But again, that person's inside of me. I just kind of have her off. One of the things we talked about was, in my performances, I always cry; I can't help it. (SInging) 'End of the World,' I start crying and she watched me on Letterman and was like, 'What are you crying about?' That song's about the world ending and me never seeing my mom again."

Lowe suggested that maybe what Parton was trying to tell her was: You need to be more professional.

"That's pretty much what she said," responded Cyrus. "She was like, 'Music is escapism. Let them cry. You need to get through it.' And I was like, 'I know, but this is who I am.' And she loved me for it," despite their different takes on how emotional to get in public. Cyrus discussed having a keen sense of how the role models she has had in her life will eventually disappear from it, as Parton has.

"I cried singing 'I Will Always Love You' with her," she said, "but I think she knew at that time that the reason I was crying is the reason that I cry now, which is because so many of my really stabilizing peers that I have in my life [come from] generations before me. And they've laid down, brick by brick, the road that I travel now. And they aren't always going to be here for me to call them and say, 'What do I do now?,' which I always did with Dolly. And she was always right. It's like how your mom's like always right, and when you're a kid, you're like, what does she know? And then as you get older, you're like, 'How? Where did this come from? You're just a normal person. Why do you know everything?' Dolly was just always right about stuff."

Cyrus' new album comes out at midnight Thursday night. She described how producer Max Martin convinced her to go for a certain upbeat and propulsive sound on the album, which she resisted, at least for songs that were conceived as ballads.

Of a track called "Aftermath," Cyrus said, "A funny story about that song: one of the lyrics actually says 'the Titan sinks,' so it was actually about a submarine, and I wrote it as a very sad ballad. I was playing a bunch of the songs that I had written, because I wrote them a little differently this record, and I was playing the record as it was with Max and I said, 'Is there anything? Like, be brutal, tell me what you don't like.' He was like, 'God, that "Aftermath" song is boring. I'm just going to be honest with you.' He's like, 'So boring.' So [I say] 'What would you do with it?' And then boom, boom, boom, boom and I was like, that is better. I was going for the Thom Yorke-like vibe, but he's like, 'No, boring.' So he made that song so much better."

articles.title: Two regular dudes are about to fish for $1.25 million against the best bass anglers in the world
articles.summary: Eric Giessing and Kyle Carr will fish against 60 elite pros including Jacob Wheeler for a record $3.25 million purse on Old Hickory Lake this fall.
articles.body: Eric Giessing and Kyle Carr are about to find out exactly how good they are at bass fishing. World Bass Enterprises (WBE) announced this week that Giessing, a 53-year-old amateur angler from Farmington, Mo., and Carr, a 39-year-old local tournament fisherman from Gatesville, Texas, have been selected as the two "Average Joes" who will compete in The Champions this fall. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS And WBE isn't sticking them in some separate amateur division. They're fishing the same tournament, for the same money, against 60 of the best professional bass anglers in the world. That includes a $3.25 million purse and $1.25 million for the winner. That’s the largest purse in bass fishing history. "Fans of every sport wonder how they'd fare competing against the pros," WBE founder and CEO Brian Bird said. "We thought it would be neat to give bass fishing fans the chance to actually answer that question. Eric and Kyle will now get to see how they stack up against the pros." Well, they're certainly going to get an answer. Here's what the 'Average Joes' are up against When Bird first told OutKick OutDoors about the Average Joes concept earlier this summer, the two spots were still up for grabs. Now we know the contestants, and WBE has since revealed the professional field they'll have to deal with. The Champions will pit its Stars and Stripes rosters against one another, bringing together elite anglers from the Bassmaster and Major League Fishing worlds. And there aren't many soft spots on either side. Start with Trey McKinney, whom OutKick OutDoors spoke with earlier this month after he wrapped up a historic Bassmaster Elite season. The 21-year-old became the youngest Bassmaster Angler of the Year in history and, at the St. Lawrence River finale, also broke the B.A.S.S. record for the heaviest one-day bag of smallmouth bass. Then there is Jordan Lee, a two-time Bassmaster Classic champion who won the sport's marquee event in consecutive years in 2017 and 2018. Hank Cherry is also a back-to-back Classic champion, while Jason Christie won the 2022 Classic. TREY MCKINNEY SAYS BASSMASTER VETERANS MADE HIM EARN THEIR RESPECT BEFORE HISTORY AOY SEASON And that's just one side of the field. The Stripes roster includes Jacob Wheeler, who has won four Bass Pro Tour Angler of the Year titles and captured REDCREST in 2026. Wheeler has racked up 12 Bass Pro Tour wins since the circuit began in 2019. There's also Dustin Connell, the only three-time REDCREST champion, and reigning 2026 Bass Pro Tour Angler of the Year Zack Birge. Oh, and Ott DeFoe, who won the 2019 Bassmaster Classic in Knoxville, is in there too. So, yeah. Good luck, fellas. The Two 'Average Joes' Aren't Exactly Beginners To be fair to Giessing and Carr, "Average Joe" doesn't mean either guy wandered into Bass Pro Shops last week and bought his first rod. Both have tournament experience. Giessing has been an amateur angler for five years and fishes primarily around Lake of the Ozarks. He started fishing as a kid with his late father and has competed in a variety of amateur events in recent years. And he's not shy about wanting to see how far he can take it. "My goal is to continue growing as a competitor, learning from every experience, and pushing myself to see how far I can take this passion," Giessing said. "I consider myself a power fisherman and enjoy the challenge of finding aggressive fish and figuring out what it takes to get them in the boat." Giessing said his ultimate goal would be reaching the professional ranks and competing at the highest level of tournament bass fishing. Well, this should be one hell of an audition. Carr also grew up fishing with his dad and now competes with Cen-Tex Bass Hunters in Belton, Texas, as well as the Tuesday Night Tight Lines 3x9 Series on Stillhouse Hollow Lake. "My dad taught me from an early age what it means to be a sportsman, respect the outdoors, and appreciate conservation," Carr said. "I've been hooked on bass fishing since I was a kid, and these days I enjoy putting that passion to work." He added: "At the end of the day, I just enjoy being on the water, chasing bass, and competing with good people who share the same passion for fishing." The jump from a Tuesday night tournament to lining up against Wheeler, McKinney, Connell and a pile of Bassmaster Classic champions is admittedly a pretty significant one. But that's also what makes this interesting. The Champions brings the two pro circuits together The inaugural Champions tournament will take place Oct. 28-Nov. 1 on Old Hickory Lake at Sanders Ferry Park in Hendersonville, Tenn., just outside Nashville. The concept from the beginning has been to put top anglers from the sport's major professional circuits on the same water and settle things in one big-money event. Bird said Giessing and Carr won't be treated any differently just because they got into the field through a sweepstakes. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER "We're going to roll out the red carpet for them and treat them the same way we treat the pro anglers," Bird said. "Both 'Average Joes' have a chance to win the grand prize and the ultimate bragging rights, but no matter what, they'll be leaving Nashville with some prize money and a great story to tell." Well, fellas, you’ve got six weeks to practice. Good luck! Love all things fishing and outdoors? Follow OutKick OutDoors on Instagram and TikTok!

articles.title: 'South Park' rebrands as 'South America' in Season 29 premiere mocking Trump's renaming push
articles.summary: "South Park" Season 29 premiered as "South America" with a renamed town sign and animated Trump, satirizing the president's renaming orders.
articles.body: Comedy Central’s "South Park" returned for its 29th season Wednesday night under a satirical new title, "South America," continuing the show’s recent run of political satire related to President Donald Trump. The premiere follows two seasons that frequently targeted Trump and his administration, including the Emmy-winning 27th season. The episode kicked off with an updated theme song referencing "South America" instead of the town’s usual name, "South Park," accompanied by a revised town sign and an animated, unclothed Trump. Later in the episode, characters wearing red and blue "South America Strong" T-shirts appeared during a country-style song celebrating the fictional rebranding. SOUTH PARK CREATORS MOCK TRUMP'S LAKE ONTARIO RENAME AND COMPANY COMPLIANCE IN MOCK STATEMENT The show also committed to the gag on its official website, changing the name and branding across much of the site and YouTube account to "South America." While the main plot centered on the town’s kids getting hooked on e-bikes, leading to Kenny’s death in an e-bike explosion, the "South America" premise satirizes Trump’s efforts to rename geographic landmarks. TRUMP FLOATS RENAMING THE ATLANTIC AND PACIFIC OCEANS AFTER REBRANDING HISTORIC LAKE Trump signed an executive order in August directing the federal government to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America." His administration previously directed the federal government to rename the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America." Ahead of the premiere, "South Park" co-creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone released a statement mocking Trump’s renaming conventions and Apple and Google’s adoption of the Lake America name. AFTER 'LAKE AMERICA,' TRUMP SUGGESTS A NEW NAME FOR THE STATE OF NEW MEXICO "Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of South Park to SOUTH AMERICA. We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount – a Skydance Capitulation," the creators said in a statement announcing the change. The joke comes after "South Park" took home an Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program, celebrating the win with another Trump joke showing a cartoon version of the president with his pants down and the caption, "You finally got your Emmy." The caption referenced Trump’s previous Emmy nominations for his reality show "The Apprentice." COLBERT WINS EMMY AFTER SHOW'S CANCELLATION BUT AVOIDS DISCUSSING TRUMP During the show’s 27th season, the writers increased their focus on Trump, beginning with the season premiere, "Sermon on the Mount," which depicted the president in a relationship with Satan. The episode won the Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program, marking the show’s first win in the category since 2013 and its first since Trump initially took office in 2017. At the time, the White House responded to the portrayal, telling Fox News Digital, "This show hasn’t been relevant for over 20 years and is hanging on by a thread with uninspired ideas in a desperate attempt for attention," White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers said. "President Trump has delivered on more promises in just six months than any other president in our country’s history, and no fourth-rate show can derail President Trump’s hot streak." Entertainment critic Christian Toto argued that the show historically targeted both sides of the political aisle but shifted its approach in its recent Trump-focused episodes. COLBERT'S FINAL YEAR MARKED BY ATTACKS ON TRUMP, LIBERAL TALKING POINTS AND CELEBS KISSING HIS RING "Last season, it abandoned that approach and went hard against all things Trump. Like many modern Trump gags, the jokes were obvious and rarely funny. In doing so, ‘South Park' earned the legacy media's newfound admiration. Suddenly, every new episode got ‘breaking news’ treatment," Toto, host of "The Hollywood in Toto Podcast," told Fox News Digital. He compared the shift to that of other major comedy shows, including "Saturday Night Live," which he said "gave up on bipartisan yuks and became a one-sided sketch factory with diminishing results." STEPHEN COLBERT'S 'LATE SHOW' JOKES TARGETED CONSERVATIVES 87% OF TIME IN FINAL YEARS, STUDY SAYS CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The first new ‘South Park’ episode of the season mostly avoided politics. We'll see if that continues. Will be interesting to see if the ensuing Trump jokes are funny or more ‘clapter,’ and if creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone return to hitting both sides of the aisle again. It's not as if they lack material on that end. James Talarico alone is worth a half dozen shows," Toto added, referencing Democratic Texas State Rep. James Talarico. Fox News Digital's Lindsay Kornick contributed to this report.

articles.title: It's been a big week for surprise celebrity babies
articles.summary: A wave of celebrity baby news is bringing some unexpected additions to famous families.
articles.body:
What do Millie Bobby Brown, Lady Gaga and Lena Dunham all have in common? They've recently welcomed babies into their families.

The Stranger Things star is the latest to expand her family, reportedly welcoming a second child via adoption with her husband, Jake Bongiovi, according to People . While neither Brown nor Bongiovi has announced the news, the 22-year-old actress appeared to hint at her growing family in an Instagram post earlier this month.

Brown shared a video in which she's seen carrying her daughter, while Bongiovi walks beside her with a baby carrier strapped to his chest. The family was shown strolling alongside alpacas in Italy's Dolomites mountain range.

The news comes a year after the couple welcomed their first daughter together , also through adoption. Brown and Bongiovi announced their decision to "embark on this beautiful next chapter of parenthood in both peace and privacy" in August 2025. In an interview with British Vogue 's December 2025 issue, Brown opened up about motherhood and explained why she and Bongiovi won't speak publicly about their daughter without her consent .

"For me, it's really important to protect her and her story until she's old enough to potentially one day share it herself," she said. "It's not my place to purposefully put her in the spotlight unwillingly. If she chooses to share her personality one day with the world, like I did when I was young, that's something we'd support. But right now, as she's so little … it's our job to protect her from that."

Lena Dunham welcomes baby girl via surrogacy

Brown isn't the only star celebrating a new arrival. In an essay published by Vogue on Wednesday, Lena Dunham announced that she and her husband, Luis Felber, have welcomed their first child, a daughter, via a surrogate. The Girls creator touched on several topics in her heartfelt essay about her journey to motherhood, writing about the first time she met her surrogate, the woes of shopping for baby clothes, the cognitive dissonance she felt over not carrying her daughter herself and the anxiety that comes with being a first-time mom.

"Even my own desire, my own long-standing and no-longer-patient readiness, hadn't prepared me," Dunham wrote. "But she was preparing herself, inside our surrogate's strong and healthy body, and as the clothes stacked up in the box, so did some sense that she was becoming real. These would be her clothes. She would be a person that we helped to dress, who made an impression on the world based on our choices, until she was old enough to do it herself."

Dunham has spoken candidly about undergoing a hysterectomy to treat debilitating pain caused by endometriosis . The Famesick author embarked on a long fertility journey with Felber, which included unsuccessful attempts at in vitro fertilization, before turning to surrogacy.

While Dunham never outright confirmed that she and Felber, whom she married in 2021, were pursuing surrogacy, she hinted at their plans of having children in a 2025 interview with the Times .

"I will say we're in the process of expanding our family in new ways," Dunham said. "I want to safely meet our children and then figure out how to talk about it."

Lady Gaga's daughter's name revealed as Rose Bean

Lady Gaga is reportedly a new mom, too. On Wednesday, TMZ reported that Gaga and her fiancé, Michael Polansky, welcomed a baby girl on June 9 in Los Angeles. Gaga and Polansky first made headlines last week after reports circulated that they'd become first-time parents.

While the Abracadabra pop star hasn't disclosed the inspiration behind her baby girl's name, Rose is reportedly inspired by the track, "La Vie en Rose," which Gaga notably covered in her 2018 film A Star Is Born , per People . Gaga also has a tattoo along her back with the phrase, "la vie en rose," in handwriting. The outlet also noted that Rose's middle name, Bean, may have been in honor of Carl Bean, an activist who inspired Gaga's famed track, "Born This Way."

articles.title: Ana Castela, Luan Santana, Panda... especialistas sugerem atrações sertanejas para o Rock in Rio  | G1
articles.standfirst: Roberto Medina disse que gênero musical está em seu radar para entrada no festival.
articles.summary: Roberto Medina disse que gênero musical está em seu radar para entrada no festival.
articles.body:
Ana Castela, Luan Santana, Panda... especialistas sugerem atrações sertaneja para o Rock in Rio — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Em 2024, o Rock in Rio fez um leve aceno (bem de leve mesmo) para o cenário sertanejo. Na ocasião, o festival incluiu o gênero no Dia Brasil, que tinha como premissa homenagear vários estilos da música brasileira e tentar tirar "as pessoas de suas bolhas", conforme explicou Roberto Medina, fundador do festival, na época.

Mas agora, Medina planeja mais. Em entrevista durante o Rock in Rio 2026, o empresário disse que ainda "não pensou nisso objetivamente", mas colocou em seu radar a presença do country e do sertanejo no evento.

"A pergunta é: por que não? O sertanejo é o gênero que é o mais tocado no Brasil, e o country é um gênero muito bacana. Então é uma coisa que está no meu radar", afirmou Medina.

Em entrevista ao g1 , ao responder a pergunta de uma frequentadora do Rock in Rio sobre a presença de Jorge e Mateus no evento , Roberta Medina, vice-presidente da Rock World (empresa que comanda o Rock in Rio), também se mostrou aberta para o gênero: "Será que vem sertanejo? Vamos ver", afirmou em tom de quem sabe que a porta está quase aberta.

Mas o que os especialistas de música acham sobre a proposta?

"Desde a primeira edição em 1985, o festival Rock in Rio se destacou pela diversidade de gêneros no line-up. Como o festival tem repercussão nacional e a música sertaneja é consumida em todos os rincões urbanos e rurais do Brasil, esse encontro precisa acontecer na edição de 2028", aponta o colunista do g1 Mauro Ferreira.

"Até porque a música sertaneja fala a língua do pop nos últimos anos", completa Mauro.

O colunista acredita também que Ana Castela e Luan Santana têm condições de apresentar grandes espetáculos inéditos no Palco Mundo. "Sem nada a dever em termos técnicos a qualquer artista internacional", aponta ele.

Para Mauro, o Palco Sunset, que costuma promover tributos, encontros inéditos e shows experimentais ( como foi o caso de Péricles cantando Motown neste ano ), poderia ser aproveitado com Daniel, Leonardo ou Panda exaltando as raízes do gênero. Ele propõe, por exemplo, um tributo a Tião Carreiro & Pardinho com Zezé Di Camargo & Luciano e Victor & Leo ( veja mais abaixo as sugestões de line-up sertanejo do Rock in Rio feita por alguns especialistas à convite do g1 ).

Para Marcos Bernardes, o Marcão do portal Blognejo, o anúncio de Medina já era esperado há algum tempo, já que o festival já se abriu para gêneros que, antes, não tinham espaço no evento, como o pagode, o forró e o brega.

"A única vez onde a gente viu ele abrir um certo espaço para o sertanejo foi no show que Chitãozinho e Xororó com algumas participações. Só que o show foi meio que apenas protocolar", recorda Marcão, citando o palco dedicado ao sertanejo no Dia Brasil em 2024.

"Para nós do sertanejo, isso ainda não é o suficiente. Então acredito que a declaração dele é a resposta a uma pressão constante. Todo ano ele fala que tem a possibilidade, todo ano ele diz que vai ter, mas ainda faltam ações mais concretas."

A dupla Chitãozinho e Xororó se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2024 — Foto: Miguel Folco/g1

Assim como Mauro, Marcão cita que o Brasil tem artistas com cacife suficiente para se apresentar no Palco Mundo e entrar para a grade do Rock in Rio.

"Basta que o Medina faça uma pesquisa um pouco maior no mercado da música de uma forma geral, que ele vai saber disso. Ele vai ter muitas sugestões positivas e, com certeza, vai sair dessa bolha que a galera, principalmente do Rio de Janeiro, sempre se encontrou, que é da bolha de não abrir tanto espaço para o sertanejo e achar que sertanejo se resume a Chitãozinho e Xororó, Zezé di Camargo e Luciano, e Leonardo."

O apresentador e influenciador sertanejo Renato Sertanejeiro diz que a proposta de Medina é válida "porque a música sertaneja é a música popular brasileira".

"Atualmente é a música mais tocada, mais executada, mais ouvida por todos os brasileiros. Seria bem legal fazer esse match entre o Rock in Rio e o sertanejo."

Para Sertanejeiro, "o Brasil é multicultural e esse match de culturas é legal".

"Acho que agregaria para ambas as partes. E pegar um dia especial e fomentar isso com o público sertanejo seria agregador para o Rock in Rio."

Panda se emociona com coro da plateira na 71ª da Festa do Peão de Barretos — Foto: Ricardo Nasi/g1

O g1 convocou alguns especialistas de música nacional e sertaneja para elencar quais poderiam ser as atrações de um possível Dia do Sertanejo. Eles citaram quatro atrações para o Palco Mundo e, outras quatro, para o Sunset.

Ana Castela é unanimidade no Palco Mundo, como é chamado o palco principal do evento e que, este ano, trouxe um telão de LED com mais de 2 mil metros quadrados, cobrindo toda sua fachada. "A Ana é a artista com maior relevância junto ao pop. Apesar das polêmicas recentes do Barretão e de coisas relacionadas à política, o fato é que o show dela é o que mais tem a ver com a cultura atual do Rock in Rio", cita Marcão.

"Ela é uma das poucas artistas da nova geração que se preocupa em incluir elementos nos shows que não são tão comuns no sertanejo, como um balé mais voltado pro pop", completa.

"O último álbum dela, que até entrou no Grammy Latino, está bem rock pop", relembra Sertanejeiro.

Luan Santana é outro que aparece na maioria das listas. "Ele conversa muito bem com artistas de outros gêneros musicais. É um cara que tem de fato condições de fazer parte do Palco Mundo de forma consistente, com show também grandioso, com grande produção, tecnológico, e num momento da carreira dele de consagração da história dele", explica Marcão.

Mauro Ferreira já deu até uma força para a curadoria de Zé Ricardo, que é conhecido por promover encontros diferenciados e inusitados no Palco Sunset.

O colunista sugeriu, por exemplo, uma dupla formada pelos sertanejos Daniel & Leonardo, reunida especialmente para o festival para reviver o repertório de Tonico & Tinoco.

Neste fim de semana, o município de Cachoeirinha , no Agreste de Pernambuco, realiza o Festival do Artesão 2026. A programação acontece no Pátio de Eventos e reúne exposição de artesanato, apresentações culturais e shows musicais no sábado (19) e domingo (20).

articles.title: Carly Rae Jepsen está em paz em ser da 'classe média do pop': 'Encontrei meu ponto ideal de sucesso' | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao g1, cantora canadense falou sobre ideia de sucesso, novo disco e última vinda ao Brasil: 'Foi uma das melhores viagens da minha vida'.
articles.summary: Ao g1, cantora canadense falou sobre ideia de sucesso, novo disco e última vinda ao Brasil: 'Foi uma das melhores viagens da minha vida'.
articles.body:
A artista canadense Carly Rae Jepsen tem um nível de sucesso peculiar: é da "classe média do pop", como chamou uma matéria do "New York Times" de 2023.

Em outras palavras, ela não está no altíssimo escalão das popstars e, para muitas pessoas, é no máximo a cantora de "Call Me Maybe". Mas para um grupo fiel de fãs, seu talento para melodias e composições no pop a colocam em um patamar diferenciado (eles não estão errados: ela é boa mesmo).

Foram esses fãs que a receberam com entusiasmo em 2023, na última vinda da cantora ao Brasil para o Primavera Sound São Paulo e show solo no Rio de Janeiro. E que aguardam ansiosamente pelo disco "Day and Night", uma incursão pela música pop da confessional à dançante, lançado nesta sexta-feira (18).

Semanas antes do lançamento, Carly conversou com o g1 sobre o álbum, a vinda em 2023 — que ela diz ter sido uma das melhores viagens de sua vida — e esse rótulo de "classe média". Veja abaixo:

Aos 40 anos e quase 20 de carreira, Carly não tem pretensões de subir ao mais altíssimo patamar do pop. "Encontrei para mim o ponto ideal de poder fazer a música que eu amo, ser capaz de viajar com ela e ter uma família e uma vida fora disso também", diz.

"Para mim, esse equilíbrio é crucial para a minha longevidade. Eu não acho que eu existiria bem em um nível onde tudo seria escrutinado e coisas sobre ser celebridade tomam o lugar da artisticidade. Isso parece um pouco invasivo para mim e um pouco demais para o que eu pessoalmente consigo aguentar. Sem julgamentos às pessoas que conseguem, eu fico impressionada e tiro o chapéu. Mas eu sinto que, conforme nós avançamos pela vida e olhamos para o que nos faz felizes e o que nos faz sentir ancorados também, o sucesso vem da sua definição. Pensei muito sobre isso literalmente desde 'Call Me Maybe' em diante".

"Me sinto realmente grata por eu ter feito essa escolha bem cedo, e sinto que eu aterrissei encontrando minha comunidade e conseguindo ter um grupo apaixonado e poderoso que eu viajo o mundo e visito cada vez que nós lançamos música, e é verdadeiramente a alegria da minha vida".

Carly Rae Jepsen em foto promocional do disco 'Day and Night' — Foto: Divulgação

Carly diz que, para este álbum, se inspirou em artistas como Minnie Riperton, Abba e a cantora de jazz Blossom Dearie. "Quando eu exploro música, eu não vou apenas atrás do que é novo. Eu realmente gosto de buscar coisas do passado que eu acho que simplesmente resistiram ao teste do tempo".

Habituada a lançar projetos duplos (seus últimos álbuns ganharam "lado A e lado B", lançados em diferentes momentos), ela decidiu colocar tudo junto desta vez em "Day and Night", que acabou ficando com 24 faixas.

Carly diz que até considerou a possibilidade de que as pessoas não ouvissem até o final, mas que, desta vez, "cada música tinha uma razão para estar lá".

"O que foi emocionante para mim foi que você pode levar o seu tempo com este álbum, que nós estávamos criando um pouco de um mundo para você existir nele, e você não tem que ouvir tudo de uma vez. Você pode fazer diferentes coisas quando você sentir vontade."

"Isso pareceu um jeito de eu poder abraçar o mundo. Ter um projeto coeso no 'day', ter um projeto coeso no 'night', e deixá-los coexistir, com esses dois sabores meio ousados que representam onde eu estou agora."

Carly Rae Jepsen em foto de divulgação de 'Day and Night' — Foto: Divulgação

Onde ela está agora é um lugar especial: a cantora se casou com o produtor Cole MGN (colaborador de "Day and Night") em 2025 e, em março de 2026, eles receberam o filho Ilya. Ou seja, há um tom de paz e alegria nesta etapa da carreira da artista — que passou toda a entrevista bastante sorridente.

Carly revela que a maior parte do álbum já havia sido concluída antes do nascimento do bebê, mas muitas músicas dão dicas desse "pequeno núcleo familiar que ela sonhava em ter um dia". "[O disco] é, sim, um retrato lindo da minha vida que eu estou muito feliz que está documentado".

Agora, ela divide o tempo entre ser mãe e promover o novo trabalho. "É louco. Quer dizer, cada parte do dia muda em torno do meu filho e nós estamos nos encaixando como uma equipe, meu marido e eu, mas é muito emocionante. Eu acho que eu não conseguiria fazer isso sem o apoio dele".

Última vinda ao Brasil teve forró e parapente

Sobre a última vinda ao Brasil, em 2023, Carly é (ainda mais) sorrisos.

"Eu estava falando disso com Cole [MGN, produtor e marido da cantora] nesta manhã. Essa foi uma das maiores viagens da nossa relação e da minha vida... Eu me senti muito livre quando eu estava lá. E eu senti que eu estava cercada por amantes da música, tipo, no show, amantes da música apaixonados e essas são as minhas pessoas. Então eu me senti muito em casa."

Segundo a cantora, o segurança que estava com a banda prometeu mostrar os lugares "não turísticos". Então, eles foram para praias secretas e saltaram de parapente.

"Quando nós estávamos no Rio, nós na verdade fomos de parapente com a pipa, fora de uma montanha, aquilo foi surreal e algo que eu sempre quis fazer e eu não posso acreditar que eu fiz porque eu meio que tenho medo de alturas."

Teve tempo para tudo: segundo a cantora, eles até saíram para dançar "uma dança coladinha, com alguns passos para lá e para cá". Em suma, pelo visto, Carly Rae Jepsen dançou forró no Brasil.

articles.title: Colin Kaepernick accuses NFL of 'colluding' against Macklemore amid 'Free Palestine' controversy
articles.summary: Colin Kaepernick accuses businessman Robert Kraft and NFL stadium owners of "openly colluding" to force Macklemore off Ed Sheeran's "Loop Tour" date.
articles.body: Former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick accused New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft and other NFL owners of "openly colluding" to force Macklemore off Ed Sheeran’s U.S. tour following the rapper’s pro-Palestinian remarks. Kaepernick drew a direct comparison between Macklemore’s removal and his own allegation that NFL owners conspired to keep him out of the league after he began protesting during the national anthem in 2016. "What Robert Kraft and what they’re saying by denying Macklemore the opportunity to go out and perform with Ed Sheeran is that they are willing to collude," Kaepernick told Ben Meiselas during a MeidasTouch interview. "They are openly colluding." MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE Macklemore had been scheduled to open for Sheeran at Gillette Stadium, which is owned by Kraft’s company, as part of the singer’s "Loop Tour." However, Macklemore said Sheeran informed him that Kraft objected to his appearance and contacted other NFL stadium owners after the rapper used his performances at MetLife Stadium to say "Free Palestine," criticize Immigration and Customs Enforcement and perform his Gaza protest song "Hind’s Hall." Kraft confirmed that Macklemore would not be allowed to perform at Gillette Stadium but disputed the suggestion that the decision was intended to silence advocacy for Palestinians. He instead cited what he characterized as Macklemore’s history of anti-Semitic rhetoric and imagery. Tour promoter Messina Touring Group subsequently removed Macklemore from the remaining dates, saying multiple venues had indicated they would not host the concerts with him on the bill. Sheeran said the decision belonged to the promoter and maintained that he had attempted to facilitate a conversation between Macklemore and Kraft. Kaepernick argued that the episode demonstrated the willingness of powerful owners to coordinate when they believe their interests are threatened. KAEPERNICK TELLS 'THE VIEW' THAT NFL OWNERS KEPT HIM OUT OVER POLITICS AND POWER, CLAIMS THEY DONATE TO TRUMP "They also want people to know that if you take an action that they don’t agree with, they will come for you," Kaepernick said. "They will organize against you, which means that we collectively have to organize to be able to protect our interests as well." "When we filed the grievance, it was like, 'well, the owners wouldn’t do that. Everybody just wants to win within the NFL,'" he added elsewhere in the interview. "And the realization is, 'no. They want to protect their interests. They want to protect their power. They want to protect their money.'" Kaepernick opted out of his contract with the San Francisco 49ers in March 2017 and has not appeared in an NFL game since the end of the 2016 season. He filed a grievance later in 2017 accusing NFL owners of colluding to prevent teams from signing him in response to his protests against police brutality and racial injustice. The league denied that its teams conspired against Kaepernick. The two sides reached a confidential settlement in 2019 without a ruling on the merits of his claim. Kaepernick also used the MeidasTouch interview to revisit the NFL’s response to the player-led protest movement. He referenced a 2017 meeting at which Buffalo Bills owner Terry Pegula reportedly said the league needed a prominent Black spokesperson to help resolve the controversy surrounding the demonstrations. Kaepernick claimed the NFL initially attempted to work through the Players Coalition before approaching him about leading its social-justice initiatives. He said he rejected the proposal and accused rapper Jay-Z of eventually stepping "into that role" through his partnership with the league. Kaepernick characterized Jay-Z as the "Black face" NFL owners sought to help "subvert the protests," arguing that the partnership redirected attention away from police killings, incarceration and resources for Black communities. The NFL and Roc Nation announced their partnership in 2019, giving Jay-Z’s company a role in the league’s live-entertainment strategy and social-justice initiative. At the time, Jay-Z said the country had moved beyond kneeling and should focus on actionable change. Macklemore, meanwhile, pledged to donate the $1 million he said he earned from Sheeran’s tour to six organizations supporting Palestinians and publicly invited Kraft to match the contribution. Kraft later said Sheeran had already privately asked him to contribute $2 million toward humanitarian relief. The remaining supporting acts on Sheeran’s tour, including Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga, withdrew amid the controversy. Kaepernick said the fallout strengthened the parallel he sees between Macklemore’s experience and his departure from the NFL. articles.title: Ms Rachel urges 'every wealthy White celebrity' to match Macklemore's donation to Palestinian causes
articles.summary: Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel vowed to match singer Macklemore's $1 million donation to Palestinian causes and urged "wealthy White" celebrities to act.
articles.body: Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel announced Thursday that she plans to match singer Macklemore's $1 million donation to Palestinian causes and urged "every wealthy White celebrity" to do the same. In an Instagram post Wednesday, Macklemore shared his plans to donate his earnings from the Loop Tour with Ed Sheeran to six organizations, including the Palestine Children's Relief Fund (PCRF), HEAL Palestine, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians, UNRWA USA National Committee and American Near East Refugee Aid (ANERA). The 43-year-old rapper was dropped from Sheeran's tour Monday after he repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" during his opening performance at MetLife Stadium earlier this month. MS RACHEL SAYS BACKLASH OVER HER GAZA POSTS 'DOESN'T FAZE' HER AS SHE CALLS OUT CELEBRITY SILENCE In response, Ms. Rachel, whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, wrote on Instagram that she plans to match Macklemore's donation and called specifically on White celebrities to do the same. "I will match Macklemore's donation and I invite every wealthy White celebrity to match it and speak out against the genocide in Gaza," Accurso wrote, adding that she will be donating to the PCRF. "Over 20,000 precious Palestinian children have been killed and children continue to be killed every day. We have a moral obligation to use our privilege and platforms to protect children and human rights." Fox News Digital reached out to Accurso for comment but did not immediately receive a response. Macklemore has challenged New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft to match his donation after Kraft refused to host the rapper at Gillette Stadium because of his activism. Kraft responded that he had already committed $2 million to Palestinian aid in the region, referencing his longtime humanitarian work in the Middle East. MS. RACHEL CLAIMS CELEBRITIES SILENT ON GAZA WOULD ‘PROBABLY’ SPEAK IF CHILDREN ‘WERE WHITE’ Accurso was also one of several prominent progressives who called out Sheeran after Macklemore's removal as the opening act for Sheeran's tour, suggesting silence to the cause was "racist." "If more than 20,000 White children were killed in another part of the world, everyone would be shouting about it at their concerts," Accurso said. "Treating some children’s lives as less worthy of outrage is racist. Silence during a genocide is not neutral." Accurso has been criticized by pro-Israel organizations and groups that say her posts have shared anti-Israel propaganda by repeatedly accusing the Jewish nation of committing "genocide." BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM Rabbi Yaakov Menken, the executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, previously said in a statement to Fox News Digital, "She claims to care about 35.5 million children suffering from acute malnutrition across Africa, the Middle East and Asia but spends an inordinate amount of time speaking about 0.031 million children in Gaza. When 0.09% of starving children receive 90% of her attention, something is wrong. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "She had nothing to say about Israeli children being held hostage until seven months later, when the backlash became too loud to ignore," he added. "It is clear that her problem is not a deep concern for children, but that she is using her purported deep concern to mask something much darker."

articles.title: MS Subbulakshmi's musical roots began at home; mother played veena, grandmother violin; how the legend got her initials
articles.summary: Music was part of MS Subbulakshmi's life long before she became one of India's most celebrated Carnatic vocalists. Born in Madurai on September 16, 19.
articles.body: Music was part of MS Subbulakshmi's life long before she became one of India's most celebrated Carnatic vocalists. Born in Madurai on September 16, 1916, the legendary singer grew up in a home filled with music. Her mother, Madurai Shanmukhavadivu, was a veena player. Her grandmother, Akkammal, played the violin.Madurai Shanmukhavadivu introduced MS Subbulakshmi to music at a very young age. The young singer's talent emerged early. Britannica reports that she recorded her first song when she was just 10. The Hindu reported that she gave her first stage performance at the age of 13.MS Subbulakshmi's musical roots in MaduraiMS Subbulakshmi belonged to the Isai Vellalar community, according to Britannica. The community had a long association with music and dance. It also included women from the Devadasi tradition. Her initials came from her mother's name, Madurai Shanmukhavadivu. This followed a naming custom associated with the tradition.Music soon became more than a family inheritance for MS Subbulakshmi. It became the foundation of an extraordinary career. By 1936 when she moved to Madras, now Chennai, she had already established herself as a promising Carnatic vocalist.Her early rise on the Madras music sceneMS Subbulakshmi's association with the Madras Music Academy marked another important stage in her career. She performed there in 1933 and was reportedly the first woman to sing at the Academy's annual conference, according to The Hindu reports.Her move to Madras also brought T Sadasivam into her life. According to The Caravan report, MS Subbulakshmi sought his help after meeting him during an earlier visit to the city. T Sadasivam was associated with the Tamil magazine Ananda Vikatan. He was also involved in the Indian independence movement.The same portal reported that T Sadasivam was married when MS Subbulakshmi came to stay with him. The two later married in July 1940, following the death of T Sadasivam's wife. T Sadasivam subsequently played a major role in managing MS Subbulakshmi's professional career.From Carnatic concerts to global stagesMS Subbulakshmi's early performances included brigas, the fast-paced musical phrases associated with the classical tradition. Over the years, devotional music became an increasingly important part of her repertoire. Her voice also reached audiences beyond traditional Carnatic music circles.The legend performed at the Edinburgh International Festival in 1963 and at the United Nations in New York in 1966. She later performed at Carnegie Hall in 1977 and London's Royal Albert Hall in 1982. Her repertoire included compositions associated with Tyagaraja, Tulsidas, Kabir, Rabindranath Tagore and Annamacharya, as reported by Britannica.Rashmika Mandanna takes on MS SubbulakshmiOn September 16, 2026, MS Subbulakshmi's 110th birth anniversary, her life received a new cinematic chapter. The biopic 'MS - A Legacy On Screen' was officially announced in Chennai. Rashmika Mandanna will portray MS Subbulakshmi in the film. The actor attended the announcement event at the Music Academy in a blue saree.Speaking about the opportunity, Rashmika Mandanna said, “I feel very proud to speak in front of you all. Right now, I have only one feeling in my heart, and that is gratitude,” as quoted by Hindustan Times.She also reflected on the legendary singer's voice, saying, “There is a unique divine power in your voice. When listening to it, I genuinely feel like I am sitting in the presence of God. It's a blessing.” Rashmika Mandanna added, “Amma, you chose me to be a small part of your life – for that, I am always grateful, and I always will be. I will definitely give my best, I promise.”Kamal Haasan encourages Rashmika MandannaKamal Haasan attended the launch as the chief guest and offered Rashmika Mandanna words of encouragement. He highlighted the importance of capturing MS Subbulakshmi's compassion through her performance.“If you bring that compassion in your eyes, you have won half the battle. You have to do it bravely,” Kamal Haasan told Rashmika Mandanna.'MS - A Legacy On Screen' is directed by Gowtam Tinnanuri, known for the National Award-winning sports drama 'Jersey'. articles.title: Investigadores chinos diseñan un tanque futurista nuclear capaz de generar su propia energía y atacar objetivos a cientos de kilómetros de distancia
articles.summary: El vehículo pesaría sobre 60 toneladas
articles.body: Un grupo de investigadores chinos ha desarrollado un tanque futurista que es capaz de tener su propia energía y atacar a objetivos a varios kilómetros de distancia. Lo han llevado a cabo con un reactor nuclear y con un cañón electromagnético. El vehículo pesaría sobre unas 60 toneladas y un pequeño reactor modular de 10 megavatios sería el que le daría la energía eléctrica. Los expertos creen que este vehículo con su cañón electromagnético podría acelerar los proyectiles a unos 3,5 km el segundo, pudiendo tener un alcance aproximado de 280 millas, en su versión final. Además, el vehículo contaría con un sistema de blindaje electromagnético y cinco toneladas de almacenamiento de energía avanzada. La primera versión tendría 10 MJ de potencia y 93 millas de alcance. Una segunda llegaría a 20 MJ y 186 millas, con más almacenamiento energético. Y a partir de 2045, incorporaría un reactor nuclear compacto para generar electricidad. El reactor de pequeñas dimensiones pretenden que quepa en tan solo dos metros cúbicos, pero los investigadores enfrentan un problema de gestión térmica, ya que el reactor produciría una cantidad considerable de calor que los ingenieros tienen que eliminar del vehículo. Por otro lado, las condiciones todoterreno también son otro problema y el pulso de disparo, por lo que serían necesario un sistema con condensadores, baterías y electrónica de potencia del vehículo. Finalmente, un experto en materia militar reveló, a South China Morning Post, que un vehículo que está tripulado con un reactor dentro y es destruido, podría generar riesgos que van más allá de lo material. Asimismo, cree que hay que darle otro enfoque y que no sea tripulado porque la tripulación necesitará descansar y los tanques seguirán requiriendo munición y mantenimiento.

articles.title: Josep Palomares, chef: "Para conseguir un buen socarrat hay que retirar la paella cuando falta un minuto"
articles.standfirst: El chef Josep Palomares explica el momento exacto para conseguir un socarrat crujiente sin quemar el arroz
articles.summary: El chef Josep Palomares explica el momento exacto para conseguir un socarrat crujiente sin quemar el arroz
articles.body: Conseguir un buen socarrat es uno de los puntos más delicados al preparar una paella. La capa de arroz tostado que queda en el fondo de la paellera es uno de los elementos más apreciados del plato, pero existe una línea muy fina entre conseguir ese punto crujiente y terminar quemando el arroz. Josep Palomares, chef del restaurante El Xiri de Monòver, en Alicante, tiene un truco para evitarlo: "retirar la paella del fuego cuando al arroz le quede aproximadamente un minuto de cocción". El cocinero explica que ese último tramo resulta determinante para conseguir el resultado que busca. "Para conseguir un buen socarrat", explica Palomares, "un truco es retirar la paella del fuego cuando al arroz le falte aproximadamente un minuto de cocción". La técnica busca aprovechar el calor acumulado en la propia paella para completar el proceso sin mantener el recipiente sobre el fuego durante demasiado tiempo. El objetivo es conseguir que la parte inferior del arroz adquiera ese aspecto tostado y ligeramente crujiente que caracteriza al socarrat, pero evitando que llegue a quemarse. Es precisamente en ese último minuto cuando el control del fuego y del calor acumulado puede marcar la diferencia. Palomares aplica este método a los arroces que prepara habitualmente en El Xiri, entre ellos el arroz con conejo y caracoles, uno de los platos destacados de su cocina. Su recomendación parte, por tanto, de una técnica que utiliza en su propio restaurante y no de una regla general aplicable de forma idéntica a todas las paellas. El socarrat no consiste simplemente en dejar el arroz sobre el fuego hasta que se queme. La intención es conseguir una capa inferior tostada y crujiente que aporte una textura diferente al resto del arroz. Por eso el momento de retirar la paella resulta tan importante. Mantenerla demasiado tiempo sobre una fuente de calor intensa puede hacer que la parte inferior pase rápidamente de estar tostada a quemarse, especialmente si ya se ha evaporado buena parte del líquido. El consejo de Palomares introduce así una modificación muy sencilla en el final de la receta: en lugar de esperar a que termine completamente el tiempo de cocción sobre el fuego, retirar la paella aproximadamente un minuto antes y dejar que el calor residual complete el proceso.
